The licensed respelling for an access that does not discharge is to declare the two bounds the rule reads: a nonnegative/min-0 and an upper bound on the index, and a mincount on the collection. Both are ordinary modifiers, available at every occasion, and neither requires a guard position — which is what makes the verdict 'yes' at the three occasions that cannot host a guard.

The respelling there is to bind the computation to a bounded field first, which is a real spelling within the surface but a less obvious one. Corpus measurement decides whether this residual is empty in practice; the verdict does not ratify on this paper argument alone.

wp.statement: 0 <= Index and Index < Items.count   (StrictlyBefore, .at / remove-at; 0 <= Index and Index <= Items.count for insert-at, IndexBoundsMode.AtOrBefore, Actions.cs:192)

cells.premiseAvailability: This is a transition-row write occasion, so the fault-family full read-set is available. The obligation has TWO independent subjects and premise availability differs per subject. The index draws its own bound from (b) an event-arg modifier (nonnegative supplies the 0 <= Index half) or from (c) a guard conjunct. The collection's cardinality is a live .count read: it is a pre-state fact (d) when the write plan does not touch Items, or a written-value fact (the 2026-07-21 carry-forward provenance) when an earlier action in the plan grows/shrinks Items. The ONLY route confirmed live to establish the RELATIONAL conjunct Index < Items.count is (c) the row guard, since neither (a) nor (b) alone can express one field bounded by another's live cardinality (verified: a statically-bounded index against a mincount-bounded collection does NOT discharge — see the computed-field cell's static probe). Under the 2026-07-21 citation duty a discharge consuming a declared collection fact (a mincount modifier, or a rule about Items.count) would have to name that fact's establishing + every preserving obligation; the built discharge below does not consume such a fact — it reads Items.count directly at the guard — so no declared-fact citation is owed by it.

dischargeContract.derivation: decompose into the two conjuncts and discharge each from declared bounds: the lower half `0 <= Index` from a declared nonnegative/min-0 on the index (a field modifier, or an arg modifier where the index is an argument), and the upper half from `hi(Index) < lo(Items.count)`, where the count lower bound is the engine's sequenced count interval seeded from the collection's declared mincount and advanced by each mutation's per-kind delta. Mode is StrictlyBefore for `.at(N)` and `remove at N`; for `insert at N` the catalog's AtOrBefore mode makes the upper test `hi(Index) <= lo(count)`, because positions 0..count are insertable.
dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: Two independent one-sided integer comparisons over already-computed intervals: read the index expression's proven interval and the collection's sequenced count interval, then test lo(Index) >= 0 and hi(Index) < lo(count) (<= for AtOrBefore). Both are finite exact-integer comparisons; reject iff either test fails or either interval is unbounded on the needed side.

dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: Normal-form match of each half against the guard's conjuncts, per disjunctive branch (a finite set); reject iff any branch leaves either half unmatched.

cells.premiseAvailability: A bare `rule` condition is anchored to no handler: it is evaluated against the whole working copy in every reachable configuration. No guard is in scope (class c unavailable), no event fired (class b unavailable), and there is no single pre-state (the condition must hold over every configuration, so class d has no distinguished predecessor to appeal to). Only class (a), field modifiers, is available — and it cannot establish the relational Items.count bound (verified: a rule condition with mincount-bounded collection and literal-max index still rejects). No discharge route exists at HEAD. (A rule may carry a `when` activation guard, which would add class (c) — but that guard conditions the rule's ACTIVATION, and a fault site inside the rule's CONDITION is evaluated wherever the rule is checked; the built engine does not treat a rule activation guard as a GuardInPath premise for a fault obligation minted in the condition. Left as the open-disposition consequence, not asserted otherwise.)
